stories.headline: CHP mayor Burcu Köksal defects to AKP, triggering party purge and street protests in Afyonkarahisar
stories.summary: Afyonkarahisar Mayor Burcu Köksal announced her resignation from CHP and joining of AKP, after days of speculation and silence. CHP responded by dismissing the local district executive board, while CHP municipal council members declared they would not follow her; protests broke out in the city and AKP official Ömer Çelik confirmed additional mayoral defections are expected next week.

stories.headline: Bahçeli proposes legal status for imprisoned PKK leader Öcalan; AKP rejects 'statü' but signals communication channel compromise
stories.summary: MHP leader Devlet Bahçeli publicly called for Öcalan to be given a legal status as 'peace and politicization coordinator' as part of the 'Terror-Free Turkey' process; AKP sources rejected the formal status proposal, saying it is legally impossible for a life-sentence prisoner, but indicated openness to expanding Öcalan's communications access. The proposal drew strong reactions from nationalist and opposition quarters, and AKP co-founder Bülent Arınç publicly challenged Bahçeli.

stories.headline: New IBB organized crime case wave: 29 arrested in Ağaç ve Peyzaj AŞ tender fraud operation, İmamoğlu weeps at ongoing trial
stories.summary: A new wave of arrests—29 detained—targeted Istanbul municipality subsidiary Ağaç ve Peyzaj AŞ over alleged rigged tender schemes; one fugitive suspect was caught on return to Turkey. Simultaneously, the ongoing IBB corruption trial's 34th hearing featured a co-defendant's son's emotional defense, prompting İmamoğlu to apologize to him 'on behalf of the state.' Antalya and other CHP mayors applied for effective remorse provisions, and testimony by CHP-linked figures implicated the party's general headquarters in a bribery claim.

stories.headline: Political espionage trial against İmamoğlu, Yanardağ and two others opens at Silivri
stories.summary: A new criminal case charging detained Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu and three co-defendants—journalist Merdan Yanardağ, adviser Necati Özkan, and Hüseyin Gün—with 'political espionage' began its first hearing at Silivri on May 10-11; prosecutors seek up to 20 years for each defendant. The case is separate from the ongoing IBB corruption trial and was triggered by statements made by Gün under an effective remorse provision.

stories.headline: SAHA 2026 international defense expo opens in Istanbul; Erdoğan touts defense industry achievements and 'Terror-Free Turkey' vision
stories.summary: Turkey's SAHA 2026 international defense, aerospace and space industry fair opened in Istanbul with over 1,700 firms from 120 countries. Erdoğan attended and delivered a major speech emphasizing Turkey's indigenous defense manufacturing achievements including drones, warships, tanks and a new hypersonic missile system; CHP leader Özel also attended. Defense Minister Güler met with MİT chief Kalın on the sidelines.

stories.headline: BARKAN 3 unmanned ground vehicle unveiled at SAHA 2026, to enter TSK inventory within two months
stories.summary: HAVELSAN debuted the BARKAN 3 autonomous unmanned ground vehicle at SAHA 2026; the company's product development director said it will enter Turkish Armed Forces inventory within one to two months. The system features autonomous mission capability, sensor and radar arrays, and can carry munitions without personnel entering operational zones.

stories.headline: Presidential decree reshuffles leadership at TCMB, TÜİK and SPK simultaneously
stories.summary: Erdoğan signed decrees published in the Official Gazette on May 9 replacing the TÜİK president (Erhan Çetinkaya dismissed, Mehmet Arabacı appointed), appointing a new SPK president (Mahmut Sütcü), and naming a new TCMB deputy governor (Yusuf Emre Akgündüz, replacing Cevdet Akçay). The simultaneous shake-up across three key economic institutions drew wide coverage and analysis suggesting Finance Minister Şimşek's influence in the appointments.

stories.headline: TCMB schedules Q2 inflation report amid rising April CPI; Goldman Sachs sees rates on hold through Q4
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Turkey announced its second 2026 inflation report presentation for May 14, to be delivered by Governor Fatih Karahan at Istanbul Finance Centre. April inflation came in at 4.18% monthly (32.37% annual), driven by energy price rises linked to the Middle East conflict; Goldman Sachs subsequently forecast that rate cuts would be delayed until Q4 2026
